item.title: Talented Guy Hovis orchestrated a memorable Neshoba County Fair day in 2000
item.description: Guy Hovis, the “other” Tupelo native whose singing talent captured national attention, passed away on Jan. 22 in Oxford at age 84. He rose to fame on the Lawrence Welk Show, combining humility, talent, enthusiasm, kindness, and generosity into a successful career and life.

item.title: Forest carbon credits for state landowners
item.description: Carbon is stored in high amounts in timber, of which Mississippi has an abundance. The state ranks in the top 10 nationally in timber production, with close to 20 million acres of timberland.

item.title: MASS announces Shape Tomorrow initiative
item.description: The Mississippi Association of School Superintendents on Friday announced the launch of Shape Tomorrow, a new statewide initiative designed to reframe how Mississippians see teaching.

item.title: Our View: Mobile sports betting sounds good, maybe too good
item.description: Mississippians wanting to bet on sports are currently restricted to doing so only in person within casinos. So naturally, tens of thousands travel out of state or participate in online sports gambling through less than legal means.

item.title: Speaker White whines about Senate killing his school choice bill
item.description: Poor Speaker White. His omnibus school choice bill got short shrift in the Senate. His resort now appears to be name calling. “Senate leadership has aligned themselves with the ACLU, Southern Poverty Law Center, the Mississippi Democratic Party, and the status quo,” he whined.
